claims.text: Human accuracy on the OpenBookQA test set reaches 91.7%.
Pre-trained science QA baselines without retraining perform near or below the 25% random guessing baseline on OpenBookQA.
Trained knowledge-free neural baselines achieve around 49% to 50% test accuracy on OpenBookQA by exploiting dataset biases.
Providing both the oracle open book science fact and author-interpreted secondary fact to a knowledge-aware neural reader increases test accuracy to 76.9%.
Incorporating retrieved ConceptNet facts alongside the core science fact decreases test accuracy compared to using the core science fact alone.

evidence.description: Human solver evaluation yields 89.3% on Dev and 91.7% on Test set.
TupleInference scored 17.9%, PMI scored 21.2%, TableILP scored 23.4%, and DGEM scored 24.4% on the OpenBookQA Test set.
Plausible Answer Detector scored 49.6%, Odd-one-out Solver scored 50.2%, and Question Match scored 50.2% on the Test set.
In oracle evaluation, the model using core fact f + secondary fact k achieves 80.2% on Dev and 76.9% on Test.
Oracle model performance dropped from 55.8% test accuracy (using core fact f alone) to 53.7% (using f + ConceptNet).

methodologies.name: OpenBookQA Dataset Construction Pipeline
methodologies.description: A multi-stage question generation and filtering process that pairs core science facts with crowdsourced common knowledge, filtered via IR/word-association solvers and crowd/expert verification.

methodologies.name: Knowledge-Enhanced BiLSTM Max-Out Reader
methodologies.description: A neural model that encodes question/choice sequences with BiLSTMs and integrates external retrieved knowledge vectors using a memory matrix attention mechanism.

limitations.text: Existing reading comprehension and QA datasets are designed to be self-contained and focus primarily on linguistic understanding rather than broad common knowledge.
The secondary facts (K) crowdsourced alongside questions were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to the question.
Retrieving external knowledge from sources like ConceptNet introduced noise and distraction that degraded model performance.

future_work.text: Solve the knowledge retrieval bottleneck in the multi-hop open book question answering setting.
Close the remaining gap between automated multi-hop reasoning systems and human-level performance on OpenBookQA.
